title: Theorem on the “universality” of the Riemann zeta-function
venue: Math. USSR-Izv. 9(3), 443–453; Russian original Izv. Akad. Nauk SSSR Ser. Mat. 39(3), 475–486
audit_scope: Checked Math-Net’s original and translation bibliographic entries and the common DOI. The English PDF retrieval was blocked, so this record does not attribute the later general compact-set formulation to the original paper.
selection_reason: The original universality work concerns uniform approximation by vertical zeta translates of a nonvanishing holomorphic target on an interior disc in the critical strip. Its role is the starting point for Bagchi’s distribution and recurrence line.

title: Recurrence in topological dynamics and the Riemann hypothesis
audit_scope: Publisher metadata, date, pages and backward references inspected. The publisher full article is subscriber-restricted in the checked route. The ISI item was inspected only as a separate archival identity and is not the source of this record.
selection_reason: The dynamical recurrence formulation links self-approximation of zeta to RH and follows Bagchi’s 1982 joint universality work. This entry identifies the recurrence journal article rather than the archival thesis.

title: On the Distribution of Spacings Between Zeros of the Zeta Function
source_edition: JSTOR scan of published article in university-hosted copy
audit_scope: JSTOR journal scan title and opening checked using page-image OCR. Numerical implementation, error certification and full figures were outside read scope.
selection_reason: Early large-scale numerical tests of Montgomery’s conjecture and GUE spacing predictions compare zeros around the origin and a much higher block. The article also identifies deviations related to primes. It is computational evidence about sampled blocks.

title: Zeros of principal L-functions and random matrix theory
audit_scope: Introduction, hypotheses and Theorems 1.1–1.2 checked in hosted manuscript; proofs and published text comparison outside scope.
selection_reason: Theorem 1.1 proves a smoothed n-level correlation asymptotic with Fourier support sum |ξ_j|<2/m for cuspidal GL(m) over Q, subject to its condition (1.7) for m>3. Theorem 1.2 adds RH for the transition to ordered normalized zeros. The support restriction is central to the GUE comparison.

title: Random Matrix Theory and ζ(1/2 + it)
audit_scope: Publisher first page, characteristic polynomial setup, and lead discussion checked. CUE derivations and the full moment conjecture proof context were outside read scope.
selection_reason: Exact finite-size Haar-unitary characteristic-polynomial moments and a Gaussian limit provide the matrix side of the moment analogy. The proposed zeta moment leading term includes an Euler product and a Barnes G-factor; the latter comes from the CUE calculation.

title: Mesoscopic fluctuations of the zeta zeros
audit_scope: All 20 pages of v1, including §§2–4 proofs, examples, diagram and references. Author-hosted version spot-checked for Corollary 1.3.
selection_reason: A joint Gaussian limit for log zeta at bounded moving shifts identifies the covariance from the logarithmic separation of the shifts. Its zero-count corollary is mesoscopic and shares the endpoint covariance structure of a Haar-unitary analogue.

title: Freezing Transition, Characteristic Polynomials of Random Matrices, and the Riemann Zeta Function
audit_scope: The four-page letter’s setup, formulas (6)–(14), proposed law and simulation summaries inspected. No independent validation of the freezing argument.
selection_reason: The short-interval maximum conjecture uses a logarithmically correlated field and predicts a −(3/4) log log log T correction to log log T on the zeta side. The freezing heuristic, Toeplitz-moment comparison and finite-height experiments are distinguished from a theorem about zeta maxima.

title: A central limit theorem for the zeroes of the zeta function
audit_scope: Theorems 1.1–1.3 and introduction checked in arXiv v5. The related DOI is reported by arXiv; proofs outside scope.
selection_reason: Theorem 1.2 extends Fujii’s mesoscopic CLT to compactly supported real bounded-variation test functions with divergent integral of |x||η̂(x)|². The random height is uniform on [T,2T], and the scale n(T) tends to infinity with n(T)=o(log T). Variance is asymptotic to that integral truncated at ±n(T).

title: Sharp conditional bounds for moments of the Riemann zeta function
audit_scope: Theorem 1 and the initial upper polynomial proposition checked. Proof of this sharp fixed-k result outside scope.
selection_reason: Assuming RH, the upper bound for the 2kth critical-line moment has the sharp order \(T(\log T)^{k^2}\) for every fixed real \(k\ge0\). Adaptive prime-block lengths remove the extra logarithmic loss from the earlier Soundararajan approach.

title: Maximum of the characteristic polynomial of random unitary matrices
audit_scope: Opening setup and Theorems 1.2–1.3 checked in primary paper; proofs and publisher-vs-arXiv comparison outside scope.
selection_reason: For Haar U(N), the full-circle maximum of the log modulus divided by log N tends to 1 in probability. The high-point set at level γ log N has logarithmic measure exponent −γ² for fixed 0<γ<1. These are matrix-ensemble results.

title: Maximum of the Riemann zeta function on a short interval of the critical line
venue: Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics 72, 500–535
audit_scope: Theorem 1.1, leading order, window and probability normalization checked in v3. Proof details outside scope.
selection_reason: Theorem 1.1 gives an unconditional leading scale log log T for the maximum of log |ζ| over |t−u|≤1 for a proportion tending to one of t in [T,2T]. It records independent conditional work by Najnudel and does not establish the FHK second-order law.

title: The Fyodorov-Hiary-Keating Conjecture. I
audit_scope: Theorem 1 and submission history checked. The [Caltech author deposit](https://authors.library.caltech.edu/records/9wk6x-70098) supplies the acknowledgment. No line-by-line reconstruction of the initial Lemma 23 or of its repair.
selection_reason: Theorem 1 supplies the upper tail C y exp(−2y) at level eʸ log T/(log log T)^{3/4}, uniformly for T≥3 and y≥1, for the maximum over |h|≤1 about a uniformly random t in [T,2T]. The author deposit acknowledges an error pointed out in the initial proof of Lemma 23. The pinned v2 receipt notes a simplified Appendix B.

title: The Fyodorov-Hiary-Keating Conjecture. II
audit_scope: Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 checked in arXiv v1. Ballot and multiscale proofs were outside scope.
selection_reason: Theorem 1 bounds the probability of the maximum falling below e⁻ʸ log T/(log log T)^{3/4} by c⁻¹y⁻ᶜ for 0<y≤(log log T)^{1/10}, T≥100. Paired with Part I this gives tightness of the recentered maximum, which is weaker than identifying its limiting law.

title: The Fyodorov-Hiary-Keating Conjecture on Mesoscopic Intervals
audit_scope: v2 Theorems 1.2–1.3 and formulas (2)–(4) checked. Publisher DOI and issue year located independently; journal proof/correction comparison and v1/v2 mathematical diff outside scope.
selection_reason: Theorem 1.2 gives an upper tail refined by the Gaussian factor exp(−y²/((1+θ)log log T)) for fixed −1<θ≤0 and y between 2 and C log log T/log log log T. The critical-line radius is (log T)^θ, with the low-prime factor Pτ(θ) multiplying the maximum. Theorem 1.3 concerns the normalized second-moment partition function.

title: Lower bounds for the large deviations and moments of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line
audit_scope: v1 Theorems 1.1 and 1.3 and comparisons to earlier bounds checked. Multiscale lower-bound proof and constants not rederived.
selection_reason: Theorem 1.1 gives an unconditional lower bound by a positive α-dependent multiple of the Gaussian tail for V∼α log log T, every fixed α>0. It complements the existing separate upper bounds and also treats primitive even characters of prime conductor at central points in Theorem 1.3.

title: Convergence in law of the maximum of the Riemann zeta function on expanding intervals near the critical line
audit_scope: Targeted dependency audit of v1 §§2–6, including assumptions, conditional local laws, annulus estimates, grid and continuum arguments, exact recentering, and final zeta transfer. Reconstructed the cited October predecessor’s unconditional approximation bridge. Selected rare-tail and fractional-moment proofs remain unverified in full. See audits/latest62_ouimet_gumbel_dependency.md.
selection_reason: Theorem 2.1 states an unconditional Gumbel limit with scale 1/(2√(1+θ)), fixed θ>0, about a uniform random height in [T,2T]. Its interval radius is (log T)^θ and its real part moves to 1/2 from the right under the prime-power cutoff and displacement hypotheses in (2.1). Centering uses an exact upper quantile in the auxiliary Haar model. This is a distinct regime from the critical-line maximum.
